title: Add Case Studies landing page + reusable customer story template
author: Ethan Wallace
description: Summary: Introduces a new /case-studies landing page in the docs site, adds a reusable Customer Story template component set (quote callouts, architecture diagram block, metrics disclaimer slot), and wires the section into the docs navigation. This PR also adds placeholder entries for upcoming stories so Sales/CS can link to stable URLs during the reference program ramp. Motivation: Marketing is standing up a customer reference + case study program for Dedicated/Private; we need a consistent, developer-first story format and a discoverable landing page that can scale beyond the first 2–3 stories. Scope: (1) New landing page with cards + filters (Deployment: Hosted/Dedicated/Private; Pillar: performance economics/reliability/deployment flexibility/ops tooling). (2) Story template MDX with required sections and default disclaimers. (3) Navigation update + sitemap inclusion. (4) Placeholder slugs for Northwind / Helios / Atlas (content is explicitly marked as “draft / coming soon” and excluded from indexing until published). Not in scope: publishing any customer names, logos, or metrics (handled in follow-up PRs once approvals land). Screenshots: included in the preview deploy comment. QA: ran local build + link check; verified nav ordering, card layout at mobile breakpoints, and that placeholder pages are noindex.
commits: docs(case-studies): add landing page route + card components
docs(case-studies): add customer story MDX template + section anchors
docs(nav): add Case Studies to primary nav + sidebar ordering
chore(ci): enable link checker to ignore draft placeholders + noindex pages
docs(content): add placeholder entries for upcoming stories (coming soon)
changed_areas: New case studies landing page and components
illustrative_snippet: Template section ordering (customer-story-template.mdx): Overview -> Problem -> Constraints -> Solution -> Implementation -> Results -> Why Redwood. Includes required blocks: (a) Metrics disclaimer (always rendered) (b) Architecture diagram slot (optional) (c) Proof/measurement notes (required if any numbers are present). Placeholder pages include frontmatter: robots: noindex, nofollow and a banner: “Customer story in progress — reach out to your AE for reference-call availability.”
review_conversation: Soojin Lee (Product Marketing) requested: (1) make “Results” optional but require “What changed + how measured” if any metric is present, (2) add approved pillar labels to prevent ad-hoc claim categories, and (3) ensure tone stays developer-first (avoid superlatives). Ethan Wallace updated template copy to include measurement notes and replaced “Results” with “Results (optional)” plus a required “Measurement notes” section when metrics are included. Camila Reyes asked to keep placeholders from being indexed/shared publicly before consent is signed; Ethan added robots noindex and removed placeholders from the landing page list unless `published: true` is set. Markus Klein flagged that the architecture block should allow both hosted and private topology diagrams and suggested adding a small caption for routing/fallback; Ethan added caption support and a default “routing/fallback policies (if applicable)” callout. Tyler Benson (Marketing Ops) asked for stable slugs and a consistent card schema for future automation; Ethan standardized frontmatter fields (title, deployment, industry, pillars, published, slug, hero_quote) and documented them at the top of the template.
checks: CI: docs-build (pass), lint (pass), typecheck (pass), unit (pass), link-check (pass after rerun). First run of link-check failed due to placeholders referencing /assets/diagrams/TBD.svg; fixed by removing asset links from placeholders and adding a TODO comment in the template with a local preview-only example.
merge_outcome: Merged via squash into main. Squash commit message: "Add Case Studies landing page + customer story template". Follow-ups tracked in DES-611 (layout polish) and ENG-9401 (docs nav final placement), and publication will happen in a separate PR once customer approvals are complete.
release_notes: Docs: Added Case Studies section with landing page + reusable customer story template (no public customer content published in this PR).
